reviews.text:
My husband and I came into the Arlington store in the middle of a torrential rainstorm, on May 16th 2020.  We had done our research and were prepared to walk out of the store as new pool owners. We were assisted by "dl"(?) And without wasting too much of his time, we put together a package of over $7k worth of goods and services.  He was not overly friendly and not very forthcoming with information. We had to prod him for options and information several times. In fact, he sold me a chemical package that I still know nothing about. But overall I suppose he was helpful and we got the deal done. I confirmed with him several times during our visit that they had the pool we settled on IN STOCK.  This information actually had an effect on which pool we were going to choose. I wanted this done asap and didn't want to wait on one to be delivered. He assured me he had at least one if not more. Little did I know at the time that it would be 6 weeks before any installer had time available...
I got on the schedule with Campbell's for Monday June 29th.  I was incredibly disappointed that I had to wait that long, but grateful that at least it would be before the 4th of July holiday. I called Bonnie and Clyde's (Arlington) right away with my install date confirmation. I also contacted Bonnie and Clyde's at least 2 other times with questions and to add more equipment to our order.  Each time, I confirmed who I was and when we were scheduled to be installed. One of those times the person on the phone had me on hold forever because they couldn't find my paperwork. They eventually found it in the TRASH. By now I'm very seriously concerned that we made a poor choice in pool companies to work with.
Campbell's contacted me a couple of times over those 6 weeks to confirm information and once even to say they wanted to do the dig EARLY to get ahead of schedule!  So they came and tore up my backyard on Saturday, June 27th, in preparation for my June 29th install.  Then about 2:30pm on Sunday, June 28th, Campbell's called me to say that Bonnie and Clyde's had no pool for them to pick up and install the next morning!!  And of course, they are so backed up with installs, that I may not be able to get another date. I was fuming! My blood pressure got so high I had to take medication to calm down. I called Bonnie and Clyde's in Arlington and immediately asked for a manager.  Corey called me back about 30 minutes later. The story that I got eventually, was that my pool was coming on the truck that was to arrive the next day Monday the 29th. The problem is that the truck wouldn't arrive until after Campbell's crew had already done their pickups for the day. Corey made no apologies whatsoever, but said she would see what she could do for another install date.  I told her it needed to be before July 3rd. Although I rather doubt it, Corey claims she called several installers and could not find another date but had worked something out with Campbell's to get me on their schedule for the following Monday, July 6th.  I told her to put me on their schedule but keep looking.
I was extremely disappointed in Corey's reaction to all of this. She was completely unapologetic, had little sense of urgency, and as a manager, took no responsibility for this huge mistake.  Why was my name not put on the pool that was in stock when I paid for it 6 weeks prior? How can you know you need something for 6 full weeks and not have it when it's due? ESPECIALLY  when you get more of them in every week!!
But let me give you some perspective:
It was the middle of summer, we had been on lock down for 4 months, and we had already waited 6 weeks for this pool to arrive so the anxiety was very high. We kept this a secret from our son for 8 weeks because it was partly a surprise for his birthday. I had company coming in town for the 4th of July and we were planning to enjoy the pool all weekend. We ended up getting installed in the rain, so the floor of the pool was too lumpy to use the expensive vacuum. And we moved before we even got it paid off. A horrible experience overall.
reviews.author: Jennifer Cooper

data.summary: Reviews appear highly authentic. They depict a typical retail pool supply store with generally helpful service but some inconsistency among staff. The detailed, specific complaints and praise read as genuine customer experiences.
authentic_signals: Specific employee names mentioned (Maddison, Chris, Cory)
Mix of ratings (5, 3) with constructive feedback
